note: Durations are [ESTIMATE] (planning figures, not measured): they assume one maintainer and the existing release cadence. Gates are the binding part: a stage is complete only when its gate check passes. Stage numbering follows docs/MIGRATION_PLAN.md. Compatibility matrix keys: old = peers/verifiers that only understand classical key exchange; new = peers/verifiers that understand the H-1 hybrid format; mixed = a fleet with both.

open_design_decisions.label: EXPLICIT OPEN DESIGN DECISION
open_design_decisions.question: Which channel distributes the peer ML-KEM public key (800 / 1184 / 1568 bytes)? Candidates: the validator manifest, the peer handshake itself (first message), or a new peer-info gossip message. The pack does not choose; the H-1 wire format is unaffected (the public key is not part of the handshake message).

open_design_decisions.label: EXPLICIT OPEN DESIGN DECISION
open_design_decisions.question: Which OpenSSL provider supplies ML-KEM to the TLS stack in stage S3 (oqs-provider vs a future OpenSSL-native implementation)? The pack does not choose; stage S3 is gated on a provider being available and audited.

open_design_decisions.label: EXPLICIT OPEN DESIGN DECISION
open_design_decisions.question: Whether authed RPC ports migrate to ML-DSA certificates (stage S3) or keep RSA certificates while only the key exchange goes post-quantum. The pack recommends keeping RSA certificates in S3 and treating ML-DSA certificates as a separate later decision.

stages.gate: A written TLS policy exists for the pinned tree: default cipher list, TLS version floor (TLS 1.2 today, TLS 1.3 allowed), and the inventory in data/tls_inventory.json is complete (27/27 checks PASS). Gate check: scripts/tls_inventory.py exits 0.
stages.name: Pin the TLS policy and finish the inventory
work: Document the current TLS surface (peer TLS, RPC/WebSocket TLS, outbound HTTPS client) from the inventory.
Record the explicit version policy: TLS 1.0/1.1 already disabled; TLS 1.2 floor; TLS 1.3 negotiable where OpenSSL offers it.
No code change in this stage.

stages.gate: The H-1 hybrid KEM wire format (docs/HYBRID_KEM.md, every byte fixed) is implemented in the peer handshake behind a feature flag, and harness/bench_hybrid.c controls C-1..C-3 pass. Gate check: reproduce.sh passes, including the hybrid controls.
stages.name: Application-layer hybrid KEM in the peer handshake
work: Implement the H-1 wire format (3-byte header + 32-byte X25519 public key + ML-KEM ciphertext) in the peer handshake.
Distribute peer ML-KEM public keys via the channel chosen in open decision D-01.
Ship peers that speak both classical-only and hybrid handshakes; hybrid is negotiated, never forced.

stages.gate: All supported peers accept hybrid handshakes and reject a hybrid envelope with a tampered or missing part. Gate check: the C-2/C-3 controls are mirrored by a peer-handshake test that rejects tampered handshakes.
stages.name: Peers require the hybrid half
work: Update peer tooling and docs to require the ML-KEM half for handshakes at or above the cutover version.
Add a policy flag: before the cutover version, classical-only is accepted with a warning; at/after it, classical-only is rejected.
Publish the cutover version and date in the release notes.

stages.gate: RPC/WebSocket TLS negotiates a post-quantum key exchange (ML-KEM via the provider chosen in D-02) in a test deployment, and the authed-certificate decision in D-03 is recorded. Gate check: a test TLS handshake completes with an ML-KEM key exchange and the handshake is captured in a log.
stages.name: TLS-stack migration (OpenSSL provider, RPC/WebSocket)
work: Load the ML-KEM provider (open decision D-02) into the TLS stack used by make_SSLContext / make_SSLContextAuthed.
Negotiate hybrid X25519+ML-KEM key exchange on secure RPC/WebSocket ports.
Decide the authed-certificate question (open decision D-03); keep RSA certificates unless ML-DSA certificates are chosen.

stages.gate: No supported release is classical-only for the peer handshake; the TLS-stack migration is reviewed against the current provider and OpenSSL versions. Gate check: repeat of the S2 and S3 gate checks on the current release.
stages.name: Review and re-evaluate
work: Re-run the full pack (reproduce.sh) against the current release.
Retire classical-only peer handshakes for new releases when the fleet allows it.
Re-evaluate the provider and certificate decisions (D-02, D-03) yearly.
